headline: Provable linear-time algorithms for snarl, superbubble, and bubble detection
label: Graph Algorithms For Genome Graphs
summary: Pangenome and phylogenetic networks require provably correct structure detection at scale, and four recent preprints supply linear-time and exact methods.
synthesis: The dominant thread is algorithmic treatment of graphs that generalize trees: pangenome graphs containing snarls, superbubbles, and bubbles, and phylogenetic networks with lateral gene transfer arcs. The snarl and superbubble preprint gives the first linear-time algorithm for identifying all snarls in pangenome graphs, plus a linear-time superbubble method via SPQR-tree decomposition. Billi formalizes panbubble and hairpin structures in cyclic pangenome bubbles, proves their strict nesting, and provides an exact method alongside a scalable heuristic. On the phylogenetic side, one study introduces an edit-operation metric comparing LGT networks with tree-based networks, and another bounds the sequence length sufficient to reconstruct level-1 semi-directed networks under the CFN model. What is new is explicit formal treatment, with proofs and tractability results, for these structures.
